title: Flat coefficient extension and the canonical cohomology adjunct
statement: Let A,E,D be commutative rings, f:A\to E and g:E\to D ring homomorphisms, with D an E-algebra and g its algebra map [def-weil-module-base-change]. Suppose D is flat over E [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let Q be any cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], K=E\otimes_A Q and T=D\otimes_A Q with coefficients through g\circ f. Let φ:K\to g_*T be a chain map satisfying φ^j(e\otimes q)=g(e)\otimes q for all j,e,q. For every integer i, the adjunction transpose of H^i(φ), followed by the exact-restriction identification H^i(g_*T)\cong g_*H^i(T), is an isomorphism D\otimes_E H^i(K)\to H^i(T). No boundedness or flatness of A\to E is required.

source.place: Tag 00HD, lemma-flat, exactness of tensor; coefficient associativity in perfect.tex Tag 0A1D, lemma-base-change-tensor. Official Stacks pages read online.

proof.text: Flatness gives preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat by RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff. Extension is a left adjoint, so also preserves finite colimits. It therefore preserves left homology data and admits the canonical mapHomologyIso. Restriction is exact as well.

Let K be extension of Q along f and T its extension along g composed with f. Mathlib extendScalarsComp.symm, mapped to complexes, gives the chain isomorphism e from extension of K along g to T. The adjoint of each e.hom.f j equals φ.f j: ExtendScalars.hom_ext reduces this to 1 tensor q, the specified formula for φ sends it to 1 tensor q, and extendScalarsComp_hom_app_one_tmul identifies the inverse associator on that generator.

In degree i let S=K.sc i and U=T.sc i, ψ the short-complex image of e.hom, h and k their chosen left homology data. Let γ be LeftHomologyMapData ψ (h.map F) k. Since ψ is an isomorphism, γ.quasiIso_iff makes γ.φH invertible. Transpose γ.φK and γ.φH by the extension/restriction adjunction. They give LeftHomologyMapData δ for the short-complex image τ of φ into U.map G: homEquiv_naturality_left and right, the component identification above, and γ.commi, γ.commf', γ.commπ prove all three required squares.

δ.homologyMap_eq and k.mapHomologyIso_eq identify the adjunct of homologyMap φ followed by the restriction homology comparison with F.map h.homologyIso.hom, then γ.φH, then k.homologyIso.inv. Apply injectivity of homEquiv, its two naturality laws, and cancel the homology-data isomorphisms to obtain this equality. Each of its three factors is an isomorphism, proving the claim.

theorem flatScalarExtensionHomologyAdjunct_isIso
    {A E D : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing E] [CommRing D]
    (f : A →+* E) (g : E →+* D) [Algebra E D]
    (hg : g = algebraMap E D) (hD : Module.Flat E D)
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (φ : ((extendScalars f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q ⟶
      ((restrictScalars g).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((extendScalars (g.comp f)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q))
    (hφ : ∀ (j : ℤ) (e : E) (q : Q.X j),
      φ.f j (e ⊗ₜ[A,f] q) = g e ⊗ₜ[A,g.comp f] q) (i : ℤ) :
    IsIso (((extendRestrictScalarsAdj g).homEquiv _ _).symm
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap φ i ≫
        (((((extendScalars (g.comp f)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q).sc i
          ).mapHomologyIso (restrictScalars g)).hom))
